target.name: Nominal
target.founder: Cameron McCord, Bryce Strauss, Jason Hoch

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $2.0B - $3.8B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Nominal is a Series B-2 stage AI & Software company currently valued at $1.0B, having raised $155M to date. The peer universe comprises 9 comparables—1 public (Palantir) and 8 private firms spanning similar sector and valuation tiers, including Ayar Labs, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach given available data. A cohort of 3 same-sector comparables at similar valuation stages yields a median valuation of $3.2B, with a range spanning $2.0B (Field AI, IPO-stage) to $3.8B (Ayar Labs, Series E). This method anchors the analysis on observable market data for direct peers rather than relying on revenue multiples or DCF assumptions not present in the dataset.

The triangulated valuation range is $2.8B (low) to $3.7B (high), with a median of $3.2B. This implies a 220% upside from Nominal's current $1.0B valuation at the median mark. Key uncertainties include the stage disparity within the peer set—Black Forest Labs at Series B provides tighter comparability than Series E or public-stage peers—and limited visibility into unit economics or revenue metrics that would refine stage-adjusted multiples. A narrower peer cohort at identical stage would reduce range uncertainty materially.
